comment: The R4 closed menu of harmless-variation / metamorphic relations, built by five parallel literature-mining passes (numerical, string/text, collections, datetime, program-text, web-API, security) and consolidated. Each entry: statement, SOUNDNESS CONDITION (checkable precondition), EXCEPTIONS (the false-alarm suppressors - load-bearing), 2 examples, sources. tier=universal holds for any correct implementation; tier=documented-property (status menu_documented) only holds when the spec asserts it. Governance per semantic-recall-brainstorm.md R4(c): entries added only with literature provenance, never from a benchmark miss; frozen before held-out; injection is deterministic by detected input kind, capped at 3, priority-ranked; the model never sees the whole menu. Full cited catalog in suites/menu-candidates.md.

entries.statement: sin(pi-x)=sin(x), sin(x+2pi)=sin(x), cos(-x)=cos(x): the documented periodic/reflection identities of the function hold.
entries.condition: The function is a genuine trig (or documented-periodic) function over radians with the standard definition.
entries.exceptions: pi is not representable so argument-reduction error requires magnitude-scaled tolerance; catastrophic reduction error at very large x; degrees-vs-radians API mismatch.

entries.statement: For a documented odd function f(-x)=-f(x); for an even function f(-x)=f(x).
entries.condition: The function is mathematically odd or even BY DEFINITION (identity of the function must be known).
entries.exceptions: signed-zero (-0.0) edge cases; asserting oddness of a non-odd function causes false accusations.

entries.statement: Applying a function then its inverse returns the input: f_inv(f(x)) = x, ON THE PRINCIPAL BRANCH ONLY.
entries.condition: STRICT: x must lie where f is injective and f_inv is the true principal inverse.
entries.exceptions: TRAP (easy to state unsoundly): asin(sin(x))=x is FALSE outside [-pi/2,pi/2]; sqrt(x*x)=|x| not x; log(exp(x)) overflows for large x; exp(log(x)) needs x>0; complex branch cuts. Restrict input to the injective domain.

entries.statement: If x1<=x2 then F(x1)<=F(x2) for a CDF; a documented-monotone function preserves (or reverses) input order.
entries.condition: The function is a CDF (monotone by definition) or documented/definitionally monotone (log, exp, sqrt on their domain).
entries.exceptions: ties allowed (<=, not <): a strict-< assertion is unsound on flat regions (discrete distributions, saturated tails); floating-point plateaus.

entries.statement: A probability distribution satisfies 0<=F(x)<=1, pdf(x)>=0, F at support-lower=0, sf(x)=1-F(x), and inverseCDF(F(x))=x on the support interior.
entries.condition: The object is a probability distribution with the standard axioms.
entries.exceptions: discrete distributions invert a step function (roundtrip lands on lattice points); 1-F(x) loses far-tail precision; inverseCumulativeProbability(0/1) may be +-inf or support bounds.

entries.statement: Shifting all inputs by c shifts location statistics (mean) by c and leaves spread (variance) invariant; scaling by c scales mean by c and variance by c^2.
entries.condition: The statistic is defined by its standard formula (mean, variance, std, median) and you know which statistic (variance is shift-invariant, mean is not).
entries.exceptions: floating-point accumulation error grows with |c| and n (magnitude-scaled tolerance); overflow when c*x exceeds range; weighted/trimmed variants may break naive invariance.

entries.statement: Reordering/reversing the input leaves the output unchanged for any order-independent aggregate (sum, product, mean, variance, min/max, gcd-of-set).
entries.condition: The function is a symmetric/order-independent aggregate. NOT for order-dependent functions (median-of-stream, cumulative sums, first/last).
entries.exceptions: floating-point sum/product are NOT associative so sum/mean/variance need tolerance; min/max/gcd are exactly invariant; NaN presence can make ordering matter.

entries.statement: det(A^T)=det(A); det(A*B)=det(A)*det(B); swapping two rows negates det; scaling a row by c scales det by c; adding a multiple of one row to another leaves det unchanged.
entries.condition: A (and B) are square; the routine computes the true determinant.
entries.exceptions: det(A*B) accumulates rounding through the product (generous magnitude-scaled tolerance; determinants can be huge/tiny); near-singular matrices amplify error; integer overflow for exact-integer routines.

entries.statement: (A^T)^T=A; (A*B)^T=B^T*A^T; A*I=A; A*A_inv=I (when invertible); trace and rank invariant under transpose.
entries.condition: conformable dimensions; inverse relations require A nonsingular (nonzero determinant).
entries.exceptions: A*A_inv=I degrades for ill-conditioned A (tolerance scaled by condition number); (A*B)^T=B^T*A^T exact only in exact arithmetic.

entries.statement: Closed-form identities: exp(a+b)=exp(a)*exp(b); log(a*b)=log(a)+log(b); Gamma(x+1)=x*Gamma(x); Gamma(n+1)=n!; B(a,b)=Gamma(a)Gamma(b)/Gamma(a+b).
entries.condition: arguments in the real domain (log/Gamma need positive / non-nonpositive-integer args).
entries.exceptions: overflow (exp(a)*exp(b) overflows before exp(a+b) via logs) - prefer logGamma/logBeta; Gamma has poles at nonpositive integers; recurrence loses precision for large x; tolerance throughout.

entries.statement: conj(z*w)=conj(z)*conj(w); |z*w|=|z|*|w|; |z|^2=z*conj(z) (real); conj(conj(z))=z; arg(z*w)=arg(z)+arg(w) mod 2pi.
entries.condition: standard complex-number semantics.
entries.exceptions: TRAP: arg/phase identities live on branch cuts - arg returns principal values, so arg(z*w) may differ from arg(z)+arg(w) by 2pi; reduce mod 2pi; infinities/NaN components; magnitude products overflow.

entries.statement: gcd(a,b)=gcd(b,a)=gcd(a,b-a); gcd(a,b)*lcm(a,b)=a*b; C(n,k)=C(n,n-k); C(n,k)=C(n-1,k-1)+C(n-1,k); n!=n*(n-1)!.
entries.condition: integer inputs in the routine's domain (0<=k<=n, non-negative for factorial).
entries.exceptions: these are EXACT (no tolerance) but OVERFLOW is the failure mode: n! and large binomials exceed long; a*b for the gcd*lcm law overflows before it is checkable - use BigInteger or bound inputs; sign conventions for gcd(0,0)/negatives differ by library.

entries.statement: A definite integral is linear and interval-additive: integral[a,c] f = integral[a,b] f + integral[b,c] f; reversing limits negates.
entries.condition: f,g integrable; for numerical quadrature the relations hold up to the method's stated error bound. Linearity/additivity are definitional; EXACT equality is documented-tolerance.
entries.exceptions: quadrature error of the split differs from the whole (use the routine's stated accuracy as tolerance); singularities at the split point; non-adaptive rules can violate additivity beyond tolerance.

entries.statement: Making an iterative/discretized computation finer (more iterations, smaller step, tighter tolerance) does not move the result away from the true answer.
entries.condition: The method is DOCUMENTED to converge under refinement (grid-refinable solver, adaptive quadrature, iterative root-finder). NOT universal - needs a documented convergence guarantee.
entries.exceptions: non-monotone convergence (error can oscillate) - compare final results within tolerance, not per-step improvement; round-off can dominate truncation past a point (finer gets worse); stopping-criterion differences.
examples: BrentSolver with tighter accuracy yields a root at least as close to the true root as a looser run

entries.statement: For an encode/decode (serialize/parse, escape/unescape) pair, decode(encode(x))=x for every x in the encoder's domain.
entries.condition: The two ops are documented inverses AND the forward op is LOSSLESS (injective). Assert the pair that starts from the encoder's native domain.
entries.exceptions: lossy/normalizing codecs (Base64 padding, URL + vs %20, JSON 1.0->1, precision loss); whitespace-trimming parsers; format(parse(s)) is generally NOT identity even when parse(format(x)) is.

entries.statement: len(a+b)=len(a)+len(b), measured in the SAME unit the function counts in.
entries.condition: Length measured in code units or bytes (additive under concatenation); concatenation triggers no normalization.
entries.exceptions: grapheme-cluster counting is NOT additive (base char + combining mark fuse); normalizing concat (NFC) can change code-point count. String.length() (UTF-16 code units) IS additive and safe.
examples: avoid asserting on BreakIterator grapheme counts

entries.condition: plain concatenation, no separator insertion, no normalization, no trimming.
entries.exceptions: join-style APIs that insert separators are NOT associative; builders that normalize.

entries.statement: join(sep, split(s,sep)) = s.
entries.condition: sep is a fixed LITERAL (not regex), occurs, and the split does NOT discard trailing empties and does NOT limit splits. Only sound if docs guarantee empties preserved.
entries.exceptions: BIGGEST false-accusation source in string testing: Java String.split(regex) drops TRAILING empties and takes a REGEX; StringUtils.split collapses adjacent separators. Use split(regex,-1) and Pattern.quote for literal delimiters.
examples: UNSOUND to flag: "a,b,,".split(",") -> [a,b] loses fields - documented Java behavior

entries.statement: reverse(reverse(s))=s, and reverse(a+b)=reverse(b)+reverse(a) (anti-homomorphism).
entries.condition: Reversal operates on a unit the double-reverse restores exactly. Code-unit reversal is self-inverse. Assert anti-homomorphism at code-unit level only.
entries.exceptions: reversing UTF-16 code units splits surrogate pairs mid-way (double-reverse still restores s, but single reverse is grapheme-wrong); combining marks migrate. Involution is safe even when single reverse is 'wrong'.

entries.statement: A case-insensitive search/compare is invariant to changing the case of query or text.
entries.condition: The op is documented case-insensitive AND case mapping is consistent (same locale both sides). Sound as a metamorphic relation (compare two runs) without an oracle for the boolean.
entries.exceptions: Locale case folding: Turkish dotless-i, German ss (length-CHANGING), Greek final sigma. toLowerCase/toUpperCase without explicit Locale use default. Case transforms are NOT length-preserving nor always round-trippable.

entries.statement: A more restrictive search/filter yields a subset; appending text to a haystack cannot remove an already-present match.
entries.condition: The added constraint is a pure conjunction/restriction, ranking/pagination held constant, search deterministic. Containment: if t.contains(x) then (t+anything).contains(x).
entries.exceptions: fuzzy/ranked search where a longer query re-scores (autocomplete, stemming); pagination truncation; stop-word removal; countMatches overlap policy.
examples: if StringUtils.contains(t,x) then StringUtils.contains(t+suffix,x) (universal for exact substring)
results('open source license') subset results('license') for exact-match

entries.statement: After r=replace(s,a,b) (all occurrences, a non-empty, b not containing a): countMatches(r,a)=0 and len(r)=len(s)+countMatches(s,a)*(len(b)-len(a)).
entries.condition: Literal (non-regex) replacement of all non-overlapping occurrences; b does not contain a; non-overlapping match semantics agreed between replace and countMatches.
entries.exceptions: regex replace with $/backreferences; b containing a (replace a->aa cascades); overlapping-match ambiguity; empty a; case-insensitive replace.
examples: trap: "aaa".replace("a","aa") - condition b not-contains a violated

entries.statement: Order-ignoring operations (sort, char-frequency, anagram, set-tokenization) are invariant under permutation of the input.
entries.condition: The op is order-insensitive by spec; comparison on the multiset/sorted form.
entries.exceptions: stable-sort tie-break observable via payload; locale collation; normalization merging code points; grapheme vs code-point for 'character frequency'.
examples: char histogram of s equals histogram of reverse(s)

entries.statement: trim(trim(s))=trim(s) (idempotent), and whitespace-ignoring ops are invariant to added leading/trailing whitespace.
entries.condition: The function is documented to strip/ignore whitespace and is idempotent. The invariance form requires docs to state whitespace is ignored.
entries.exceptions: String.trim() strips only <=U+0020, NOT Unicode whitespace (NBSP); strip() does. A patch moving trim->strip changes output legitimately. Significant-whitespace formats (YAML, Python).

entries.statement: A normalizer is idempotent: norm(norm(x))=norm(x); canonically-equivalent inputs normalize equal.
entries.condition: The function is documented as a canonicalizer/normalizer (Unicode NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD, path canonicalization, whitespace collapsing). Idempotence guaranteed by the Unicode spec.
entries.exceptions: NFC/NFD change length and code-point count (length equality UNSOUND); NFKC/NFKD are lossy; concat does not distribute over normalization at the seam.

entries.statement: unescape(escape(x))=x, AND the escaped output embedded in its target grammar parses back to literal x (no injection).
entries.condition: Docs name a specific escaping scheme (HTML, XML, JSON, CSV, SQL-literal, regex-quote) and its matching unescaper. Round-trip only guaranteed encoder->decoder.
entries.exceptions: escapers are usually NOT idempotent (double-escaping & -> & -> &amp;) - never assert escaper idempotence; many-to-one decoding; context-sensitive escaping (HTML attr vs text vs URL vs JS).

entries.statement: parse(format(x))=x for a formatter/parser pair with the SAME locale, pattern, and rounding.
entries.condition: Docs specify the format is reversible and both sides share locale + pattern + precision.
entries.exceptions: locale mismatch (, vs . decimal separator); rounding/precision loss (#.## drops digits); grouping separators; currency symbols; date formats without year/timezone; format(parse(s)) normalizes and is usually NOT identity.
examples: trap: format US then parse GERMANY -> wrong value

entries.statement: Adding one element increases size by exactly one (bag) or zero-or-one (set), never decreases it, never removes a present element.
entries.condition: size before/after and membership of untouched elements both checkable. Bag (List): size +1. Set/keyed (Set/Map): +1 iff element absent, else equal.
entries.exceptions: bounded/capacity structures with eviction (LRU, ring buffers); Set.add returns false on duplicate; List.add(index,e) still +1.

entries.statement: Removing an element decreases size by at most one, never introduces new elements; removed element absent (set) or count-1 (bag).
entries.condition: removal target present. Set: size-1 and !contains. Bag: exactly one occurrence removed (List.remove(Object) removes FIRST).
entries.exceptions: List.remove(Object) vs remove(int) overload ambiguity; removeAll removes every occurrence; removing absent element is a no-op.

entries.statement: A query documented as read-only leaves all observable state unchanged: size, capacity, contents, iteration order, internal position/capacity identical before and after.
entries.condition: The method is a pure accessor per contract (size, contains, get, peek, indexOf, charAt, length, capacity). Compare a deep snapshot before vs after.
entries.exceptions: documented lazy/caching accessors that legitimately mutate (access-order LinkedHashMap.get reorders BY CONTRACT - gate it out); iterators advancing position are not read-only.
examples: int c=sb.capacity(); sb.charAt(3); assert sb.capacity()==c && sb.length()==len (a read-only StrBuilder query must not grow the buffer)

entries.statement: Two API entry points documented to compute the same thing return equal results on the same input: overloads, convenience wrappers, default-argument forms.
entries.condition: The two methods are specified as equivalent (one delegates to / is a special case of the other). Identical arguments; assert equal outputs and equal resulting state.
entries.exceptions: overloads with genuinely different contracts (remove(int) vs remove(Object)); primitive-vs-boxed autoboxing; default charset/locale differences.
examples: Collections.sort(list) equals list.sort(null); String.indexOf(s) equals indexOf(s,0)

entries.statement: For distinct keys/elements, insertion order does not affect the final container: insert(a);insert(b) == insert(b);insert(a).
entries.condition: DISTINCT keys and set/keyed semantics. Equality by abstraction (entrySet/toList canonicalized).
entries.exceptions: same-key collision -> last-write-wins makes order matter; LinkedHashMap/LinkedHashSet preserve insertion order so toList differs though key-set equal; Map.merge/putIfAbsent order-sensitive.
examples: trap: use equals() not iteration order for LinkedHashSet

entries.statement: Applying a documented normalizing operation twice equals once: sort(sort(xs))=sort(xs), distinct twice = once, trim twice = once.
entries.condition: The op is genuinely idempotent (sort, dedupe/distinct, Set construction, trim, canonical-format). NOT for accumulating ops.
entries.exceptions: unstable sort may reorder equal elements on the second pass (equal as bag, differing identity); locale case-folding edge cases.

entries.statement: Combining with the empty/identity element is a no-op, and combination is associative: concat(x,empty)=x, concat(concat(a,b),c)=concat(a,concat(b,c)).
entries.condition: The op forms a monoid (list concat, append, Set union, addAll, sum/product). Identity is []/""/emptySet/0/1. Commutativity ONLY for set-union / abelian aggregation - NOT list concat or string append.
entries.exceptions: non-associative combiners (float sum); bounded capacity truncating on overflow; Set union commutes but list concat does not.

entries.statement: An operation followed by its inverse returns to the original (bag/value-wise): pop(push(s,e))=s, remove(add(c,x))~=c, reverse(reverse(xs))=xs.
entries.condition: A true inverse exists. Bag/value equality, not identity.
entries.exceptions: lossy operations (dedupe, toLowerCase have no inverse); capacity growth from push not undone by pop (compare contents, not capacity); add-then-remove of a duplicate in a set vs bag differs.

entries.statement: The result equals that computed by a trivially-correct reference model (linear scan / sorted association list) under an abstraction function.
entries.condition: A simpler obvious-correct oracle exists. Abstraction applied to BOTH sides (compare toList outputs, not internal layout). Model must match set-vs-bag semantics.
entries.exceptions: model must agree on the SAME semantic; ordering of toList for unordered structures canonicalized (sort) before comparison.
examples: map.get(k) equals linear scan over assocList
sources: Hughes, How to Specify It! (model-based properties)

entries.statement: Strengthening a query with a conjunctive filter yields a subset (size non-increasing); relaxing with a disjunctive clause yields a superset.
entries.condition: DOCUMENTED filter/query semantics with no side effects. filter(p AND q) subset filter(p).
entries.exceptions: non-deterministic ordering/pagination limits; filters with side effects; short-circuit predicates that mutate; capacity-limited results.
examples: xs.stream().filter(p.and(q)).toList() is a subsequence of filter(p).toList()
adding a WHERE clause returns a subset of rows

entries.statement: Partitioning and recombining conserves count: |filter(p)|+|filter(not p)|=|all|; size(a)+size(b)=size(concat(a,b)) for bags; |A union B|=|A|+|B|-|A intersect B| for sets.
entries.condition: Bag vs set is decisive: bag concat adds counts; set union uses inclusion-exclusion. Partition predicate total and side-effect-free.
entries.exceptions: overlapping partitions double-count; groupingBy key collision; set dedupe drops the additive law; capacity truncation.
examples: set trap: setA.size()+setB.size() != union.size() when overlapping

entries.statement: Operations documented to preserve an order actually preserve it: a stable sort keeps relative order of equal-key elements; LinkedHashMap preserves insertion order.
entries.condition: ONLY when the contract promises the order (the counterpart trap to permutation-invariance).
entries.exceptions: Arrays.sort(primitive[]) is NOT stable (dual-pivot quicksort); HashMap/HashSet promise no order; parallel streams may reorder.
examples: Collections.sort(list,byKey) keeps prior relative order of equal-key records
trap: Arrays.sort(int[]) gives no stability guarantee

entries.statement: The same physical instant rendered in two time zones represents the same timeline point: comparing them as instants yields equal; only wall-clock fields differ.
entries.condition: Comparison at the INSTANT (epoch-millis/Instant/UTC) level, not local-field. Type must be instant-carrying (DateTime, Instant, ZonedDateTime) - NOT a local/partial type.
entries.exceptions: LocalDateTime/LocalDate/Partial carry no zone so are legitimately unequal as instants (category error, not a bug); leap-second smearing; different tzdata versions disagree on historical offsets.
examples: the same instant in America/New_York and Europe/London compares equal via isEqual

entries.statement: Formatting a temporal value with formatter F and parsing back with the same F reproduces the original (parse(format(x))=x).
entries.condition: F must be LOSSLESS for the type (include every field: zone/offset for ZonedDateTime, fractional seconds) and use a fixed explicit Locale and zone.
entries.exceptions: locale-dependent formatting (month/day names, AM/PM); lossy patterns (dropping zone); zone abbreviations (EST) ambiguous; DST-overlap wall times; format(parse(s)) fails for non-canonical valid text.
examples: a pattern lacking an offset must NOT be asserted to round-trip a zoned value

entries.statement: Adding a strictly positive EXACT duration (fixed nanos/millis) to an instant moves it strictly forward; x.plus(d) > x and x.plus(d).minus(d)=x.
entries.condition: Use a MACHINE-TIME duration (Joda/java.time Duration - fixed elapsed) applied to an INSTANT type. Distinguish from calendar amounts (Period, months/days).
entries.exceptions: TRAP: for zone-aware local-time arithmetic, adding a Period of '1 hour' across a DST gap/overlap does NOT add fixed elapsed time (spring-forward=23h, fall-back=25h) so wall-clock can appear non-monotonic; adding months/years is not reversible (Jan31+1month=Feb28); overflow at min/max instant; leap seconds.
examples: instant.plus(Duration.standardHours(1)) is strictly after instant, always
across fall-back, localDateTime.plusHours(1) can repeat a wall time - legitimately

entries.statement: Converting a set of instants into any common zone preserves their pairwise ordering and pairwise elapsed durations (Duration.between is zone-invariant at the instant level).
entries.condition: Comparison and duration computed on instants. All values converted to the same target zone (or kept as instants).
entries.exceptions: wall-clock FIELD differences are NOT preserved across a DST transition (two instants 1h apart can show same or 2h wall gap); assert instant arithmetic only.
examples: if instant a<b in UTC then a<b viewed in Asia/Kolkata
Duration.between(a,b) identical regardless of display zone

entries.statement: A local wall time in a spring-forward GAP corresponds to no instant; a wall time in a fall-back OVERLAP corresponds to two; a correct patch handles these per the library's documented resolution policy, not by assuming a bijection.
entries.condition: Applies only to zone-aware construction from local fields. You must know the library's policy (Joda throws/adjusts; java.time ZonedDateTime.of shifts gap times forward).
entries.exceptions: THIS IS THE EXCEPTION SET for the other datetime relations: Joda throwing IllegalInstantException on a gap is CORRECT, not a regression; java.time pushing a gap time forward; overlap resolving to earlier offset by default.
examples: constructing 02:30 on US spring-forward day in America/New_York is illegal/shifted - not a round-trip failure
01:30 on fall-back maps to two instants differing by the DST offset

entries.statement: Feb 29 exists iff the year is a leap year (ISO/Gregorian rule); day-of-year has 366 in leap years; plusYears(n) on Feb 29 lands on Feb 28 in a non-leap target.
entries.condition: Use the chronology the value is expressed in (ISO/Gregorian, Julian differ). Leap SECONDS are separate and unsupported in Joda.
entries.exceptions: non-ISO chronologies (Julian pre-1582, Islamic) have different leap rules; Feb29+1year clamping to Feb28 is not reversible; Julian->Gregorian cutover dates.
examples: new LocalDate(2000,2,29) valid; 2001-02-29 must be rejected

entries.statement: For a fixed input I, deleting statements that I never executes yields a program that produces identical output for that same I under a correct compiler; a mismatch signals miscompilation.
entries.condition: Deadness established by PROFILING the actual execution of I (coverage), not static analysis. Equivalence claimed only for input I. Program deterministic and free of undefined behavior.
entries.exceptions: UNDEFINED/unspecified behavior (uninitialized reads, signed overflow, strict-aliasing) voids the guarantee - the #1 EMI false positive; non-determinism; timing/__LINE__ reflective values; stack-layout perturbation of UB-dependent output.
examples: EMI/Orion: pruning a branch input I never takes must not change I's output
removing an unexecuted loop body leaves the same result for the profiled input

entries.statement: Inserting syntactically valid code into a region unreachable under input I must not change I's output under a correct compiler.
entries.condition: Insertion site must be provably-under-profile dead for I, or guarded by a predicate false at runtime for I. Inserted code well-defined if ever reached.
entries.exceptions: if inserted code has side effects reachable under I (opaque predicate the optimizer folds), divergence is expected; UB inside inserted code; insertion changing code size shifting UB-sensitive behavior.
examples: Athena: MCMC-guided insertion into dead blocks preserves I's behavior
wrapping junk in if(opaque_false){...} must not alter output

entries.statement: Mutating LIVE code in a value-preserving way (equivalence-preserving rewrites of executed statements) must not change I's observable output.
entries.condition: Each mutation must be semantically value-preserving on the live path (identity-net-effect statements, proven-equal expression replacement). Stronger precondition than dead-code because the code runs.
entries.exceptions: UB introduced by the rewrite; floating-point reassociation/contraction (FMA, -ffast-math) legitimately changing results; integer overflow in the rewritten expression; volatile/atomic ordering.
examples: Hermes: injecting live statements that recompute and restore a variable's value preserves output
replacing x*2 with x+x on integers where no overflow occurs

entries.statement: Inserting insignificant whitespace or comments must not change the SEMANTIC result: same token stream (modulo trivia), same AST, same diagnostic SET by rule/category, same compiled behavior.
entries.condition: The trivia must be genuinely insignificant for that language and position: not inside a string/char literal, not splitting a token, and the language not whitespace/indentation-significant at that point.
entries.exceptions: CRITICAL: line-number/column/offset fields in diagnostics and AST node positions legitimately change with inserted newlines - compare diagnostic IDENTITY/COUNT, not positions; indentation-significant languages (Python, YAML, Haskell, Makefiles); minifiers, normalizing/style-preserving printers; preprocessor token-pasting.
examples: inserting a /* comment */ between two statements must not change the number or category of diagnostics
a linter's warning COUNT is invariant to comments though warning line numbers shift

entries.statement: A code formatter is idempotent (fmt(fmt(x))=fmt(x)) and semantics-preserving: parse(fmt(x)) yields an AST equivalent to parse(x); for a parser, unparse(parse(s)) re-parses to an equivalent AST.
entries.condition: Formatter claims idempotence/stability. Equivalence at the SEMANTIC AST level (ignoring trivia/positions), not text identity.
entries.exceptions: style-preserving vs normalizing printers differ (a normalizer changes text on first pass but must be idempotent after); comment reflow may not be text-idempotent; trailing-comma/quote normalization changes bytes not semantics; version-upgrade non-idempotence expected.
examples: formatting must not change the program's runtime behavior (AST-equivalent)

entries.statement: Adding a conjunctive filter never enlarges the result set (filtered output is a subset); adding a disjunctive OR term never shrinks it.
entries.condition: The added parameter is documented as a pure result filter (does not change ranking or the queried collection); both requests run against the same data snapshot and authorization scope.
entries.exceptions: pagination caps (compare full sets/totals, not one page); top-N ranking cutoff pushing a legitimate item out of view; eventual-consistency churn between calls; personalized/randomized ranking.
examples: GET /items?status=open returns a subset of GET /items
adding a second keyword yields count(new) <= count(old)

entries.statement: Re-issuing a query with a different sort criterion returns the same SET of items (order aside).
entries.condition: The sort attribute is documented display-only and does not interact with a truncating limit; the full result set is compared (not one ranked page).
entries.exceptions: paginated/top-N responses where sorting changes which items land on page one; ties broken non-deterministically; a sort key that is also a filter.
examples: search ordered by date vs by rating returns the same video set
GET /hotels?city=London sorted by price vs by score returns the same hotels

entries.statement: Omitting a parameter with a documented default produces output IDENTICAL to explicitly passing that default; equivalently-expressed inputs (1MB == 1024KB) produce identical output.
entries.condition: The parameter's default is documented and stable; no other implicit context (time, personalization) differs.
entries.exceptions: server-side default varying by client/locale/experiment; non-deterministic default ordering; time-sensitive defaults.
examples: search with no order equals search with order=relevance (the documented default)
search with no page size equals limit=20
sources: Segura et al. MET 2019 (Input equivalence MRP)

entries.statement: Two queries differing only by mutually exclusive values of the same attribute return disjoint result sets.
entries.condition: The partitioning attribute is single-valued per item and its values are exclusive per the data model.
entries.exceptions: multi-valued attributes (an item legitimately in two categories); overlapping ranges; items re-classified between calls.
examples: GET /refunds?status=COMPLETED and status=CANCELLED share no items
sources: Segura et al. MET 2019 (Disjoint partitions MRP)

entries.statement: When an attribute's value domain fully partitions the data, the union of per-value follow-up outputs equals the unfiltered source output; optionally |S|=sum|Fi|.
entries.condition: The partition is both disjoint AND exhaustive - every item falls in exactly one bucket (no uncategorized residue).
entries.exceptions: items outside all named buckets (disjoint but not complete); pagination truncating a sub-query; data changing mid-sequence.
examples: videoDuration short union medium union long = all videos for a keyword
orders filtered by each status value, unioned, equal all orders
sources: Segura et al. MET 2019 (Complete partitions MRP)

entries.statement: For a partitioning attribute, the source output minus the union of some value-buckets equals the union of the remaining buckets.
entries.condition: Disjoint + exhaustive domain; set difference computed on stable identifiers.
entries.exceptions: residual uncategorized items; pagination cutoffs; churn.
examples: all testing videos minus long videos = medium union short videos
all orders minus (shipped union delivered) = pending union cancelled
sources: Segura et al. MET 2019 (Partition difference MRP)

entries.statement: Replaying a request that reaches a protected resource, changed only so a user lacking that privilege (or another user's object id) issues it, must NOT return the same protected content - it must yield an error or a different output.
entries.condition: The system documents role/ownership-based authorization for that resource; the source action legitimately retrieved it; the URL is a real resource. Guard with cannotReachThroughGUI / userCanAccess preconditions (as SMRL does).
entries.exceptions: intentionally public/shared resources; an admin follow-up user who legitimately has access (exclude admins via a user precondition); resources identical for all users by design.
examples: changing only the user id / object id in a URL must not grant access to another user's data (IDOR, CWE-286)
a link from an admin interface, requested by a non-admin, must return an error
sources: Bayati Chaleshtari et al. TSE 2023 (MST-wi/SMRL, pattern P1)

entries.statement: Modifying only one parameter to contain a malicious payload must be neutralized (output equal to the benign case) OR lead to an error - the injected code's effect must never be observable.
entries.condition: The mutated field is user-controlled input reflected/stored by the system; the source action succeeded benignly; the oracle observes where the payload's effect would surface. Avoid actions whose normal output is already an error.
entries.exceptions: fields documented to accept raw markup (rich-text editors); benign inputs coincidentally matching the attack detector; response non-determinism unrelated to the payload.
examples: concatenate ' OR '1'='1 into a field - must not alter query results (CWE-89)
sources: Bayati Chaleshtari et al. TSE 2023 (pattern P2)

entries.statement: After any authentication-state-changing action (login, sign-up) the session identifier must change; session tokens must not be reusable across the boundary.
entries.condition: The system documents session-based auth via cookies; the actions occur after a login boundary.
entries.exceptions: stateless (token-per-request) auth with no server session id; deliberate SSO flows preserving a session; documented long-lived 'remember me' sessions.
examples: the session id after login must differ from the pre-login session id (session fixation, OWASP OTG-SESS-003)
session variables/cookies must not be reused after logout

entries.statement: Removing a mandatory prerequisite action from a source sequence and replaying the rest must fail - a later action must not succeed when a required earlier step was skipped.
entries.condition: The business logic documents an ordered precondition (step B requires step A); the source sequence executed A then B successfully.
entries.exceptions: steps documented as optional; idempotent re-entry points; prerequisite satisfiable out-of-band.
examples: register->confirm email->login succeeds, but register->login (skipping confirmation) must be rejected (CWE-841)
checkout must not complete if payment-authorization is dropped
sources: Bayati Chaleshtari et al. TSE 2023 (CWE_841, subset-of-actions follow-ups)

entries.statement: Requesting a credential-bearing or session-setting endpoint over an unencrypted channel must not transmit credentials in cleartext and must set protective cookie attributes.
entries.condition: The system documents that authentication endpoints require HTTPS and that session cookies carry Secure/HttpOnly flags.
entries.exceptions: endpoints explicitly documented as public/non-authenticated; TLS-terminating proxies where the app legitimately sees HTTP internally (test at the edge).
examples: login credentials must never be sent over an unencrypted channel
session cookies must carry Secure/HttpOnly attributes
sources: Bayati Chaleshtari et al. TSE 2023 (OWASP config/session mapping)

entries.statement: Adding environment or repetition actions must trigger the documented control: N failed logins lock the account; a simulated time delay forces a password change; a state-changing POST without a valid anti-CSRF token is rejected.
entries.condition: The system documents a lockout threshold, password-aging window, usage cap, or CSRF-token requirement.
entries.exceptions: controls intentionally disabled in the tested config; accounts exempt from lockout (service accounts); a legitimate rate-limit response that itself looks like an error IS the expected outcome, not a failure.
examples: advance the clock a year after login - the next action must prompt a credential change (CWE-262/263/309/324)
replay a state-changing request without the CSRF token - must be rejected
sources: Bayati Chaleshtari et al. TSE 2023 (Fig.16, added DelayAction)
